operators.name: Identity operator

operators.section: A. Structural operators, projectors, and transfer
operators.name: Coefficient metric transport
operators.scope: Finite presentations of one physical inner-product space in orthonormal physical coordinates. For a physical metric $Q$, use $H_X=S_X^*QS_X$. Its kernel is $\ker S_X$ when $Q$ is positive definite.

operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: A. Structural operators, projectors, and transfer
operators.name: Transported bilinear form
operators.scope: Fixed invertible coordinate change $C$. For a complex Hermitian form use $H\mapsto C^{-*}HC^{-1}$, where $C^{-*}=(C^{-1})^*$.

operators.section: B. Cyclic, spectral, and arithmetic projectors
operators.name: Residue coefficient projector
operators.scope: Formal series; $N\ge1$
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: B. Cyclic, spectral, and arithmetic projectors
operators.name: Roots-of-unity projector
operators.scope: Field containing a primitive Nth root of unity, with N nonzero and invertible. Coefficient masking OP-025 does not require roots of unity.
operators.review_note: The displayed Fourier projector needs inverses of N and the cyclotomic character orthogonality law.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: B. Cyclic, spectral, and arithmetic projectors
operators.name: One-dimensional character projector
operators.scope: Finite group G, a complex representation rho and a one-dimensional character chi. The result is algebraically idempotent; it is an orthogonal projection when rho is unitary.
operators.review_note: The formula applies to a one-dimensional character of any finite group, not only a cyclic group.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: B. Cyclic, spectral, and arithmetic projectors
operators.name: Multi-index residue projector
operators.scope: Independent multivariate coefficient coordinates, or explicitly commuting residue selectors. Each modulus is positive.
operators.review_note: Products of selectors are projectors only with the requisite commutation, supplied here by independent coordinates.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: B. Cyclic, spectral, and arithmetic projectors
operators.name: Polynomial spectral projector
operators.scope: Finite operator whose minimal polynomial splits with no repeated roots. The listed lambdas are all its distinct eigenvalues.
operators.review_note: Distinct eigenvalues in the formula mean distinct spectral values. Diagonalizability is essential for this simple Lagrange formula.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: B. Cyclic, spectral, and arithmetic projectors
operators.name: Cyclic product routing
operators.scope: Formal series over commutative ring
operators.review_note: The sum is over the finite residue set. All cross-packet products, including carries, are retained.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: B. Cyclic, spectral, and arithmetic projectors
operators.name: Differentiation residue transport
operators.scope: Formal derivatives; residue indices modulo $N$
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: B. Cyclic, spectral, and arithmetic projectors
operators.name: Translation packet transfer
operators.scope: Polynomial coefficients; generally mixes residue packets
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: B. Cyclic, spectral, and arithmetic projectors
operators.name: Residue refinement
operators.scope: Coefficient projection for integer $M\ge1$
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: B. Cyclic, spectral, and arithmetic projectors
operators.name: CRT idempotent selector
operators.scope: Pairwise coprime positive moduli m_i with M their product. The e_i are the CRT idempotents. P_i is linear over Z/MZ.
operators.review_note: The operator is multiplication by an idempotent class, not the scalar class in isolation.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: B. Cyclic, spectral, and arithmetic projectors
operators.name: CRT reconstruction
operators.scope: Product of rings $\mathbb Z/m_i\mathbb Z$ for pairwise coprime $m_i$, with $M=\prod_i m_i$. The output is a class modulo $M$, not a unique unrestricted integer.
operators.review_note: CRT reconstruction is a ring isomorphism and a Z-module map. It is not a vector-space change over mismatched fields.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: B. Cyclic, spectral, and arithmetic projectors
operators.name: Cartier decimation
operators.scope: Formal series over a declared coefficient ring, integer radix p>=2 and 0<=r<p. No characteristic-p hypothesis is needed for decimation itself.
operators.review_note: Decimation reindexes retained coefficients. It is not the same as the degree-preserving projector OP-025.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: B. Cyclic, spectral, and arithmetic projectors
operators.name: Frobenius endomorphism
operators.scope: Commutative ring of prime characteristic $p$. Frobenius is $\mathbb F_p$-linear and is an automorphism on finite fields. Relative to a larger field of scalars it is generally semilinear.
operators.review_note: Primality and commutativity are needed for the standard Frobenius ring endomorphism. Over extension fields it need not be linear over that whole field.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: B. Cyclic, spectral, and arithmetic projectors
operators.name: Finite-field packet selector
operators.scope: Specified finite-field vector space and idempotent endomorphism. Specialization of OP-009.
operators.review_note: This is a finite-field specialization of the general idempotent operator, not a separately counted new discovery.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: B. Cyclic, spectral, and arithmetic projectors
operators.name: Finite group representation projector
operators.scope: Irreducible complex character $\chi_\rho$ of dimension $d_\rho$ and a finite representation $U$. The projector selects the isotypic component. It is orthogonal if $U$ is unitary.
operators.review_note: The dimension factor is for an irreducible character. Unitarity distinguishes orthogonal from merely algebraic projection.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Coordinate change
operators.scope: Square invertible basis matrices for the same finite dimensional space. A rectangular full-column-rank basis is not inverted as a square matrix.
operators.review_note: The inverse formula presupposes square bases of the same space. Rectangular subspace charts require a different coordinate solve.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Monomial to falling-factorial transport
operators.scope: Polynomial rings over any commutative unital coefficient ring. The basis matrix and inverse are unitriangular with integer entries. Newton quotient and spectral interpolation formulas require additional units.
operators.review_note: $\Phi$ is a linear isomorphism in positive characteristic too. It is not an algebra homomorphism for ordinary multiplication.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Stirling second-kind transform
operators.scope: Locally finite sequence transform. For polynomial coefficients $a_n$, the falling-factorial coefficients are $b_k=\sum_{n=k}^{d}S(n,k)a_n$. This uses the transposed index orientation.
operators.review_note: This entry is the lower-triangular sequence transform. Polynomial coordinate conversion uses the transposed index orientation.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Signed Stirling first-kind inverse
operators.scope: Inverse of the lower-triangular sequence transform OP-042. Polynomial coordinate conversion uses the corresponding upper-triangular connection matrix.
operators.review_note: As for OP-042, do not identify sequence-matrix orientation with polynomial coefficient orientation.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.name: Binomial transform
operators.scope: Sequences with triangular exact coefficients
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Inverse binomial transform
operators.scope: Finite triangular inverse
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Lah coordinate transform
operators.scope: Coefficients a_n in the rising-factorial basis become b_k in the falling-factorial basis through degree d.
operators.review_note: The original sequence formula did not give the claimed polynomial coordinate conversion. The source uses row k, column n equal to L(n,k).

operators.name: Forward finite difference
operators.scope: Polynomial or sequence carrier

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Newton sample-difference transform
operators.scope: Polynomials of degree at most $d$ over a $\mathbb Q$-algebra. The binomial coefficient is $d_k$ and the falling-factorial coefficient is $d_k/k!$. This quotient is not valid where $k!$ is a nonunit.
operators.review_note: Forward differences are coefficients of binomial polynomials. Falling-factorial coefficients require division by k!.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Divisor Möbius inversion
operators.scope: Arithmetic functions on divisibility poset
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Subset zeta transform and Mobius inverse
operators.scope: Finite Boolean subset lattice with coefficients in a commutative ring.
operators.review_note: The displayed forward sum was a zeta transform, not the signed Mobius inverse. Both directions are now explicit.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Ordinary to exponential coefficient normalization
operators.scope: Q-algebra, or a finite degree range in which every required factorial is a unit. There is no general invertible ordinary/EGF normalization in characteristic p at degree p and above.
operators.review_note: Invertibility of factorial normalization is stronger than characteristic zero. Divided-power multiplication in characteristic p does not make this change of basis invertible.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: General normalized basis transport
operators.scope: Same finite polynomial or series truncation with invertible gamma_n and eta_n in the coefficient ring.
operators.review_note: Normalizers must be units in the actual coefficient ring, not merely nonzero formal labels.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Formal derivative
operators.scope: Degree bounded polynomial maps $\mathcal P_n\to\mathcal P_{n-1}$
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Basepoint antiderivative
operators.scope: Polynomial map P_{n-1} to P_n over Q or a Q-algebra, with declared basepoint a. Output has value zero at a.
operators.review_note: Antidifferentiation divides by positive integers. A Q-algebra supplies these inverses.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Point evaluation
operators.scope: Polynomial covector; exact rational $a$
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Interval integration functional
operators.scope: Finite rational polynomial spaces, rational endpoints and fixed rational density. For a positive-measure interpretation impose a<=b and rho>=0.
operators.review_note: The linear functional exists for signed constant densities as well. Nonnegative density is needed only for measure-positivity interpretations.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Integration-constant defect projector
operators.scope: Polynomials of degree at most $n$ over a $\mathbf Q$-algebra, or over a coefficient ring where the denominators used by $J_a$ are units. The derivative lowers the degree bound and $J_a$ restores it with value zero at $a$.
operators.review_note: The defect operator is I-JD, rather than JD itself. Its image is the constants.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Affine pullback
operators.scope: Polynomial carrier over a declared field, with fixed a,b. Invertible exactly when a!=0 on the full polynomial coordinate change.
operators.review_note: Pullback is linear in f even though the input substitution is affine. Invertibility additionally requires nonzero slope.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Multiplication by coordinate
operators.scope: Polynomial degree grows by one
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Formal composition operator
operators.scope: For infinite formal series require g(0)=0. Polynomial outer functions can be substituted more generally. A finite jet substitution must respect its truncation ideal.
operators.review_note: An arbitrary infinite formal composition is not defined at a nonzero constant term without extra convergence or nilpotence assumptions.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Shift polynomial
operators.scope: Canonical coefficient shift $L$; finite polynomial
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Appell basis change
operators.scope: Polynomial coefficient ring with the needed binomial identities and a_0 a unit. The displayed family is triangular with leading coefficient a_0.
operators.review_note: An Appell sequence is a basis only with a nonzero, invertible leading normalization.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Recurrence companion transfer
operators.kind: affine state update; joint linear map
operators.scope: Fixed companion matrix C. Forcing u_n may be fixed externally, or included as a separate input. Homogeneous update uses u_n=0.
operators.review_note: A fixed nonzero forcing term makes the state update affine, not linear. Joint dependence on state and forcing is linear.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Recurrence defect extraction
operators.scope: Finite stream and prescribed recurrence coefficients
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Formal series reciprocal
operators.scope: Unit formal series; constant coefficient invertible
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Formal logarithm operator
operators.scope: Q-algebra with u(0)=0, or a declared finite truncation in which each required denominator k is invertible.
operators.review_note: Characteristic zero alone does not guarantee that 1/k exists in the coefficient ring.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Hurwitz product
operators.scope: Sequences over a commutative ring, with integer binomial structure constants. The ordinary analytic EGF interpretation requires its own normalization and convergence hypotheses.
operators.review_note: Hurwitz multiplication can be defined directly by integer binomial coefficients, even when formal factorial denominators do not exist.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: D. Prime-power and digit operators
operators.name: Prime-power reduction
operators.scope: Prime $p$ and positive depth $r$
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: D. Prime-power and digit operators
operators.name: Truncated local p-adic coefficient operator
operators.scope: Integral coefficients reduced modulo a declared prime power p^r. It is not a precision-raising map.
operators.review_note: This is coefficientwise application of OP-068, with a Z-module rather than field-linear interpretation.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: D. Prime-power and digit operators
operators.name: Local Mahler mask transform
operators.scope: Normalized unit mask R in 1+z A[[z]] over a commutative ring A, with integer radix p>=2. Each coefficient stabilizes after finitely many factors.
operators.review_note: The infinite formal product needs R(0)=1. An arbitrary invertible constant term is insufficient.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: D. Prime-power and digit operators
operators.name: Local mask recovery
operators.scope: Formal unit F over a commutative ring. This is inverse to OP-070 on normalized series F(0)=1. Otherwise retain F(0) as separate data.
operators.review_note: The quotient loses F(0). It reconstructs F/F(0), not an arbitrary unnormalized unit series.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: D. Prime-power and digit operators
operators.name: Digit carry transfer matrix
operators.scope: Finite normalized local mask R with r_0=1, radix p>=2, digits 0<=d
operators.review_note: The carry state set and terminal convention are part of the representation.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: D. Prime-power and digit operators
operators.name: Cartier linear representation
operators.scope: Fixed boundary vectors and transition matrices. The digit order is least significant first. The representation and its zero-index convention must be declared.
operators.review_note: Reading a digit word is a scalar evaluation of a represented state, not a linear map of the integer index n.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: D. Prime-power and digit operators

operators.name: Finite convex gauge operator
operators.scope: Finite dimensional real space and convex absorbing K with 0 in its interior. A compact K symmetric about the origin gives a norm; without symmetry the gauge may be asymmetric.
operators.review_note: A general convex gauge is not a norm without balance or symmetry. In the symmetric real case it is a norm.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: I. Computational and finite model operators
operators.name: K-COS coefficient extraction
operators.scope: Integrable f on [a,b], a<b. Reconstruction uses c_0/2 plus the nonzero cosine terms where convergence is justified. Finite truncation and tail or floating-point error require separate bounds.
operators.review_note: The zero-frequency coefficient is half-weighted in the cosine reconstruction. Exact interval coefficients must not be conflated with characteristic-function approximations.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: J. Finite arithmetic and representation models
operators.name: Finite Frobenius action
operators.scope: A declared finite linear model over a specified fixed field. If Frobenius acts on extension-field scalars, record F(av)=sigma(a)F(v) instead of asserting full-field linearity.
operators.review_note: A chosen Frobenius element acts linearly through the declared representation. This is not automatically the scalar power map $x\mapsto x^p$ in OP-037.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: J. Finite arithmetic and representation models
operators.name: Finite monodromy operator
operators.scope: Specified finite dimensional representation with nilpotent N. Any relation to Frobenius and its normalization must be stated separately.
operators.review_note: Monodromy data require nilpotence and any Frobenius compatibility convention from the actual representation.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: J. Finite arithmetic and representation models
operators.name: Finite cochain coboundary
operators.scope: Explicit finite cochain complex over a declared ring or field. The displayed condition is not automatic for arbitrary linear maps.
operators.review_note: A cochain differential has degree +1 and compatible adjacent types. Squaring to zero is a family condition.
operators.source_relationship: retained catalog entry, with source routes

operators.section: A. Structural operators, projectors, and transfer
operators.name: Synthesis-kernel projector
operators.scope: Finite maps $A_X:X\to K_X$, $S_X:K_X\to X$ with $S_XA_X=I_X$.
operators.review_note: This complementary idempotent isolates coefficient changes invisible to synthesis. It is generally oblique, not an orthogonal projector.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: A. Structural operators, projectors, and transfer
operators.name: Two-endpoint coordinate transport
operators.scope: $T:X\to Y$ may be rectangular. $C_X$ and $C_Y$ are invertible coordinate changes on the source and target separately.
operators.review_note: Similarity is the endomorphism specialization. A rectangular map cannot be transported using one arbitrary conjugating matrix.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Covector pullback
operators.scope: $A:X\to Y$ fixed and $\ell\in Y^*$. Pullback needs no inverse. For a change $y=Cx$, the same functional has target row $\ell C^{-1}$.
operators.review_note: Pulling a functional back along a map is not the same direction as changing the coordinates used to store that functional.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Falling-factorial residue projector
operators.scope: $m\ge1$ and $0\le r<m$. The map $P_r^{(m)}$ selects monomial degrees modulo $m$ and $\Phi(z^k)=x^{\underline{k}}$. Finite polynomial coefficients over a commutative ring suffice.
operators.review_note: Its labels are falling-factorial degrees, not ordinary powers of x. It survives even where a particular spectral interpolation formula fails.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Transported polynomial product
operators.scope: Polynomial ring and invertible linear basis map $\Phi$. Multiplication is performed before transport.
operators.review_note: For the falling-factorial map, $x\star x=x(x-1)$. The operator $\Delta$ is a derivation for $\star$, not for ordinary multiplication.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Falling-factorial raising operator
operators.scope: Polynomial ring over a commutative coefficient ring. The map $R$ raises the degree bound by one. For the degree-$d$ square truncation in the falling-factorial basis, $[\Delta_d,R_d]=I-(d+1)E_d$, where $E_d$ projects onto the top basis vector.
operators.review_note: $R x^{\underline{k}}=x^{\underline{k+1}}$ and $[\Delta,R]=I$ on the polynomial ring. This is not multiplication by $x$ alone. The finite boundary term vanishes when the coefficient ring kills $d+1$, including in characteristic dividing $d+1$.
operators.source_relationship: explicit consequence of the source basis and transported-product laws

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Falling-factorial degree operator
operators.scope: Polynomial ring with declared coefficient characteristic. It has eigenvalue $k$ on $x^{\underline{k}}$.
operators.review_note: Spectral interpolation through degree d needs the differences $k-j$ to be units. In characteristic p, degree labels can collide while coefficient projectors remain distinct.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Formal compositional inversion
operators.scope: $\phi(0)=0$ and the coefficient of z is a unit. Finite jets use equality modulo $z^{N+1}$.
operators.review_note: This is inversion under substitution, not reciprocal multiplication. A vanishing linear coefficient must not be accepted as an invertible chart.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Recurrence reconstruction
operators.kind: linear in initial data and defects
operators.scope: Fixed order $d\ge1$, finite horizon and recurrence coefficients. The input contains all d initial values and every required defect.
operators.review_note: With the defects retained this reconstructs arbitrary finite sequences. Dropping them changes the problem to a homogeneous recurrence.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: G. Dynamics, inference, and elimination
operators.name: Finite observability operator
operators.scope: Fixed finite state transition A, observation C, horizon $m\ge1$, and zero input or known input contribution subtracted.
operators.review_note: Exact state recovery requires full column rank. A long observation list alone does not imply observability.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: G. Dynamics, inference, and elimination
operators.name: Finite controllability operator
operators.scope: Fixed finite A and B, horizon $m\ge1$, zero initial state. For nonzero initial state add $A^m x_0$.
operators.review_note: The displayed order is chronological input order. Reversing columns without reversing inputs changes the action.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: J. Finite arithmetic and representation models
operators.name: Finite trace observation
operators.scope: Supplied finite matrix whose columns are declared constituent trace lists. The scalar field and selected rows are fixed.
operators.review_note: This measures finite linear combinations. It does not establish an arithmetic identification outside the supplied places.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: J. Finite arithmetic and representation models
operators.name: Trace-table reconstruction
operators.kind: linear on the image; guarded recovery
operators.scope: A has r columns and full column rank. Observations must belong to its image. Recovery is for the selected trace rows.
operators.review_note: The source selects independent rows. Unused observations need a separate consistency check. A rational solution is not automatically an integral nonnegative multiplicity vector.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: I. Computational and finite model operators
operators.name: Joint query encoding
operators.kind: map; linear when the queries are linear
operators.scope: For linear maps the displayed kernels are subspaces. For general maps read the equality as intersection of fiber-equivalence relations.
operators.review_note: The joint observation retains both queries. It need not retain all information about the original object or every future query.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: I. Computational and finite model operators
operators.name: Descended coarse operator
operators.scope: Surjective linear observation $q:X\to Y$. A unique $\overline T$ exists exactly when $T(\ker q)\subseteq\ker q$.
operators.review_note: Pointwise recovery of one query is weaker than closure under all future updates. The kernel condition is necessary and sufficient here.
operators.source_relationship: linear specialization of the source fiber-factorization criterion

operators.section: K. Metric transport and compatibility
operators.name: Metric adjoint
operators.scope: Positive-definite Hermitian metrics on finite source and target spaces. Here star means the raw conjugate transpose in the stored coordinates.
operators.review_note: A singular coefficient metric cannot be inverted this way. Pass to the synthesis quotient or use an explicitly justified generalized inverse.
operators.source_relationship: explicit finite-dimensional consequence of the source metric-pairing laws

operators.section: K. Metric transport and compatibility
operators.name: Metric-whitened representation
operators.scope: Positive-definite finite metrics and invertible metric factors. The underlying map is typed between those metric spaces.
operators.review_note: Changing metric factors changes B only by unitary factors. It does not change its singular values.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: K. Metric transport and compatibility
operators.name: Intrinsic distortion functional
operators.scope: Invertible map between spaces of the same finite dimension $n\ge1$, with positive-definite Hermitian metrics. Singular maps do not receive a finite value under this contract.
operators.review_note: Distortion is submultiplicative. Its logarithm is subadditive, not an exact additive cocycle.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: K. Metric transport and compatibility
operators.name: Determinant normalization
operators.scope: Invertible n by n real or complex matrix, $n\ge1$. The positive real nth root is used.
operators.review_note: This sets determinant modulus to one. A negative real determinant or complex phase is not changed to +1. It removes volume scale, not shear.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: K. Metric transport and compatibility
operators.name: Conformal metric residual
operators.kind: linear in the metric pair for fixed T and scale; quadratic-affine in T
operators.scope: Fixed finite map T, positive scale $\lambda$, and positive-definite metrics for the geometric interpretation.
operators.review_note: A zero residual certifies that edge under the chosen data. Common metric completion requires compatible equations across all relevant paths.
operators.source_relationship: residual form of the source conformal metric equation

operators.section: K. Metric transport and compatibility
operators.name: Metric holonomy residual
operators.scope: Finite holonomy H and positive-definite Hermitian root metric Q. The result is the squared metric Hilbert–Schmidt norm.
operators.review_note: Coordinate invariance transports both $H\mapsto gHg^{-1}$ and $Q\mapsto g^{-*}Qg^{-1}$. Keeping Q fixed gives a different comparison.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: K. Metric transport and compatibility
operators.name: Metric propagation along an edge
operators.kind: linear in the metric for fixed edge
operators.scope: Invertible finite edge T and positive-definite source metric. This is the isometric scale-one convention.
operators.review_note: Propagation along a path is exact. Distinct paths give the same metric only when their loop holonomy preserves the root metric.
operators.source_relationship: explicit rearrangement of the source metric-compatibility equation

operators.section: K. Metric transport and compatibility
operators.name: Quadratic metric-defect composition
operators.scope: $\mathcal E(T)=T^*Q_YT-Q_X$ for composable finite maps $T:X\to Y$ and $U:Y\to Z$, with the same intermediate metric.
operators.review_note: This is an exact matrix identity. It is distinct from the scalar log-distortion inequality. Dropping the pullback factor gives a false law.
operators.source_relationship: derived composition identity proved in this compendium, not a claim of a new source theorem

operators.section: L. Finite integration and observation
operators.name: Atomic integration functional
operators.scope: Fixed finite nodes and weights. Nonnegative weights define a positive atomic measure. Signed weights define a functional without an automatic positivity claim.
operators.review_note: Vector-valued finite sums are interpreted componentwise. Exact arithmetic applies only to exact supplied evaluations and weights.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: L. Finite integration and observation
operators.name: Moment integration covector
operators.scope: Finite polynomial support and exact known moments. In a different polynomial basis the covector must be transformed with the basis witness.
operators.review_note: For monomial-to-basis synthesis B, the row is m transposed times B. Arbitrary weights labelled with a basis name are not a basis proof.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: L. Finite integration and observation
operators.name: Finite measure pushforward
operators.kind: linear in the measure for fixed map
operators.scope: Finite atomic measures, or the declared exact affine polynomial setting. The source does not implement arbitrary nonlinear change-of-variables certification.
operators.review_note: Noninjective maps may merge atoms and still preserve mass. A density formula requires additional hypotheses.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: L. Finite integration and observation
operators.name: Partial integration on a product
operators.scope: Finite polynomial p and supplied product measures with the required moments. Finite atomic products and bounded rational interval products are covered.
operators.review_note: The remaining x dependence is retained. A general joint measure cannot be replaced by a product of marginals without changing its correlations.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: L. Finite integration and observation
operators.name: Signed quadrature functional
operators.scope: Fixed finite nodes and possibly signed weights. Exact evaluation of the sum is distinct from equality with a target integral.
operators.review_note: A degree-of-exactness certificate compares moments. It does not certify all functions or every higher polynomial degree.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: L. Finite integration and observation
operators.name: Moment discrepancy functional
operators.scope: Fixed measure, quadrature rule, and finite polynomial space. Every basis moment in that space must be checked.
operators.review_note: The functional vanishes on the whole space exactly when its moment residual vector is zero. One successful integrand is not sufficient.
operators.source_relationship: explicit residual form of the source moment-exactness criterion

operators.section: L. Finite integration and observation
operators.name: Fixed-weight derivative averaging
operators.kind: linear in a family of providers
operators.scope: Finite compatible differentiable maps, fixed parameter-independent weights, matching domains, target shapes, and derivative order.
operators.review_note: Moving weights require extra product-rule terms. The source adapter intentionally does not supply differentiation of a varying measure.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: L. Finite integration and observation
operators.name: Integration-by-parts boundary functional
operators.scope: Polynomials on $[a,b]$ and constant density $\rho$. Integration by parts states $I(fg')+I(f'g)=\mathcal B(f,g)$.
operators.review_note: The boundary term is part of the operator identity. Dropping it changes the bilinear pairing.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: L. Finite integration and observation
operators.name: Affine density transport
operators.kind: linear in the source measure for fixed affine map
operators.scope: $a\le b$, $\rho\ge0$ and $s\ne0$. The image interval is ordered increasingly. At $s=0$, the pushforward is an atom, not this density.
operators.review_note: Absolute slope is required for a positive measure. Oriented integration is a different convention.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: A. Structural operators, projectors, and transfer
operators.name: Canonical dual frame synthesis
operators.scope: Finite full-column-rank analysis A with specified inner products and orthonormal stored coordinates for this formula.
operators.review_note: This is the general frame construction behind OP-094. It is not counted as an inequivalent primitive. Rank-deficient A requires a different reconstruction claim.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Formal exponential
operators.scope: Commutative $\mathbb Q$-algebra and $u(0)=0$, or an explicitly finite nilpotent/truncated setting with all required factorials invertible.
operators.review_note: The exponential and formal logarithm are inverse on the stated classes. Formal coefficient identities do not require numerical convergence.
operators.source_relationship: documented formal operation; standard coefficient definition supplied explicitly

operators.section: C. Coordinate, polynomial, and sequence transforms
operators.name: Normalized coefficient multiplication
operators.scope: Basis $e_n=z^n/\gamma_n$ over a ring where the indicated normalizers are units. Integral structure constants may alternatively define a divided-power algebra.
operators.review_note: Hurwitz multiplication is the factorial case. An integral divided-power product need not imply an invertible normalization to ordinary power-series coordinates.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

operators.section: E. Signal, wavelet, and polyphase operators
operators.name: Causal recursive filter
operators.scope: Fixed finite coefficients with $a_0$ invertible and a declared input/output prehistory. Finite output is computed recursively.
operators.review_note: Nonzero fixed continuation state makes the input-to-output map affine. Carrying that state is necessary for chunk equivalence. A finite run does not prove stability.
operators.source_relationship: explicit source construction

relations.law_tex: (\exists!\,\overline T:Y\to Y\text{ linear}:\overline Tq=qT)\iff T(\ker q)\subseteq\ker q

relations.name: Coarse defect composition
relations.assumptions: Use typed maps $T:X\to Y$ and $U:Y\to Z$, observations $q_X,q_Y,q_Z$, and proposed coarse maps $\overline T,\overline U$. Define $E_T=q_YT-\overline Tq_X$, $E_U=q_ZU-\overline Uq_Y$, and $E_{UT}=q_ZUT-(\overline U\overline T)q_X$. The displayed law uses the composed coarse candidate $\overline U\overline T$. An independently proposed $\overline{UT}$ contributes the extra term $(\overline U\overline T-\overline{UT})q_X$.

relations.name: Metric whitening

editorial_corrections.note: Kernel preservation is equivalent to existence and uniqueness of an induced coarse map. It does not validate an arbitrary supplied candidate.
Polynomial integration requires a rational coefficient algebra or invertible integration denominators.
Residue packets use a positive modulus, normalized labels, and shifted labels read modulo that modulus.
The finite raising/lowering boundary is $(d+1)E_d$, which can vanish in characteristics dividing $d+1$.
The singular-value distortion contract requires positive dimension and compatible positive metrics.
